absent: Exact numeric values of extended feature masks, MWAIT leaf constants, substate mask, idle override codes and capability numbers.
Implementations of monitor wait, guest aware halt and default halt idle handlers and of hypervisor default override.
Layout of debugger regset tables and software bytes area beyond mask storage.
Definitions of capability word counts, leaf two record structure and cache and TLB type enumerations.
Full CPUID parse list beyond basic leaves zero and one, leaves structure layout and reset and fill helpers.
Cyrix configuration register numbers, access semantics and clock string usage.
Boot option storage, sibling thread counting and static call registration details.

findings.text: Init time configuration updates debugger register descriptors for extended state using a total byte size and a mask, adjusting 64 bit and 32 bit compatibility views where compiled and storing the mask in a software reserved word indexed by USER_XSTATE_XCR0_WORD.
Boot time entry selects the idle handler for subsequent idle threads, preserving a polling choice or an earlier installation when present and otherwise installing one of the halt based variants.

Selection retains the current handler when polling override IDLE_POLL is active, with a one time notice if threaded sibling count indicates multithreading under symmetric multiprocessing, and also retains any handler already registered to respect a hypervisor default, only choosing anew when neither retention applies.

Usability of monitor wait for idle depends on absence of any command override, presence of MWAIT support, absence of MONITOR and AMD APIC C1E defects, and CPUID MWAIT leaf showing either no extension requirement or at least one C1 substate.
Readiness test reports true once an idle implementation has been registered through the static call mechanism, allowing later selection logic to avoid overwriting it.

Host default for extended state omits user dynamic mask XFEATURE_MASK_USER_DYNAMIC together with guest supervisor mask XFEATURE_MASK_GUEST_SUPERVISOR, while guest default omits only the dynamic mask, making the host enabled set narrower than the guest enabled set.
Early parameter handler consumes a string option, clearing broadcast invalidation support when the text requests IPI mode and unconditionally signalling that the option was handled.

Processor vendor descriptor carries a vendor label with up to two identification strings and a numeric vendor code, plus distinct callbacks for early setup and boot processor setup and general setup and identification and TLB discovery, extended on 32 bit builds with a cache sizing callback and five family mapping records each pairing a family number with sixteen model names.
Vendor registration places the descriptor address into a dedicated init section so boot code can enumerate supported vendors without explicit listing.
Feature dependency record stores a feature number alongside the number of the feature it requires.
Static dependency list expresses prerequisite relationships among capability bits and ends with an empty record that terminates traversal.

Floating point capability underlies FXSR save support, which underlies CMOV and MMX and basic vector levels, with wider levels building stepwise from XMM toward XMM2 and then AVX families and their specialized variants for neural, fused, crypto and 512 bit forms.

Extended save capability XSAVE underlies its optimized and compact and supervised variants as well as key protection and matrix tile enablement through faulting and tile stages, with additional dependencies for command submission and shadow stack on the supervised variant.

Platform quality, enclave, control and invalidation features follow their own prerequisites, with monitoring and allocation subfeatures requiring their base, enclave leaves requiring SGX and its first version, and LASS, FRED, SSBD and INVLPGB each requiring their respective base capability.
Total count of feature plus bug bits is computed from the numbers of capability and bug words scaled to bit units.

Descriptor translation table maps CPUID leaf two codes to cache or TLB characteristics, covering instruction and data and unified levels with sizes from kilobytes to tens of megabytes and translation entries from a handful to about a thousand, with unlisted codes remaining zero.
Cache initializers record a cache kind with a kilobyte size while translation initializers record a translation kind with an entry count, both keyed by descriptor value.
Parser output pairs a register block pointer with a leaf accounting pointer for the reader to fill.
Parse record holds leaf identity and start subleaf, offsets for register and info storage, a slot capacity, and a reader routine receiving the record and the output pair.

Builder macros fill a parse record from leaf and suffix by deriving offsets and capacity from the leaves collection and attaching the named reader, including a form that picks the first subleaf for the leaf.
Helper macros obtain byte offsets of register and info fields and the element count of a register array for a given leaf suffix inside the leaves aggregate.

Generic subleaf reader iterates from the configured start across the configured capacity, fetching each subleaf into successive register slots and incrementing the stored count; the global reader list itself is generated from a central macro table.
Partial CPU scan first clears the requested leaf interval and then repopulates it, with interval refresh delegating to that scan and single leaf refresh delegating to interval refresh.
Reversed bounds or bounds crossing CPUID range classes cause a one time warning and no table change.
External callers may request cached CPUID data to be rebuilt for a single leaf or for an inclusive leaf interval of one processor description.
Legacy identification wrapper preserves interrupt state across the configuration register probe by saving flags on entry and restoring them on exit.

Probe starts by testing writability of one configuration register to detect device identification support, then either reads two identification bytes when supported or toggles a second configuration bit to separate earliest steppings, always leaving registers as found.
Toggling configuration bits without restoration or concurrent access during the probe could alter processor setup, hence the need for bus settling reads and interrupt exclusion.

Static tables translate direction and family codes into part names for 486 class and 6x86 class members and into clock multiplier characters, with one retained byte holding part of the probed direction value.

Idle configuration begins unset, transitions to retained when polling is forced or a handler already exists, otherwise moves to one of monitor wait, guest aware halt or default halt with the first applicable choice winning.
Leaf two table contains two hundred fifty six slots addressed directly by descriptor byte value.
Number of debugger visible 64 bit units for extended state equals total size divided into eight byte pieces.
Both CPU headers employ single inclusion guards defined once per translation unit.
Central parse table begins with generic readers for the first two basic leaves, with further entries defined beyond the visible portion.
